Subject: Carex Health — BAA availability and PHI deployment clearances (post-demo)

Hi Jill — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side after the demo: 

- BAA availability: we can sign a standard Redwood BAA for Carex. Attached is a copy of our current BAA template and SOC 2 report for initial review (SOC2_Report_2026.pdf, BAA_Templates.zip).
- PHI handling: from the demo notes, Carex intends to surface patient identifiers and visit summaries to the model for chart summarization. For clarity: hosted/shared Redwood API (multi-tenant hosted endpoints) is not eligible for PHI. Eligible options are Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools, tenant-isolated) or Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) depending on your network and key management needs.
- Questionnaire and evidence: you mentioned a vendor security questionnaire — we can start that immediately. I've attached a blank Carex_Vendor_Questionnaire.xlsx that we filled with answers where obvious; please flag any items to escalate to our security team.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Confirm which deployment mode you'd like us to evaluate (Dedicated vs Private) — if you need an estimate for Dedicated sizing we can provide that in the next 48 hours.
2) Procurement: loop in procurement@carexhealth.com if you want us to start contracting + DocuSign for the BAA.
3) Security questionnaire: confirm a point of contact and we'll return completed answers and supporting artifacts (SOC2 PDF + logs retention policy) by EOD Monday.

If you'd like, we can also set a 30-min follow-up with our security lead (Karthik) to go through the questionnaire items that are likely to require clarifications (encryption, key management, audit logs).

Thanks — looking forward to the next steps.

Best,

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Confirming scope: our pilot will process PHI (patient names, MRNs, visit notes) for automated chart summarization and coding suggestions. We cannot use multi-tenant/shared endpoints for this workload.
2) Deployment preference: we would prefer Dedicated if Redwood can provide tenant isolation, strict network egress controls, and KMS integration (we use AWS KMS). If Dedicated requires network peering changes, our infra team will coordinate.
3) Security questionnaire: attaching a procurement-level questionnaire — procurement@carexhealth.com will own contract negotiations. 

Can you confirm the following items before procurement moves forward: 
- SOC 2 Type II availability window (dates covered) — I see the SOC2_Report_2026.pdf but want to confirm coverage period.
- Does Redwood support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) for Dedicated?
- What is the minimum contract term for Dedicated and typical provisioning lead time?

If Karthik is available next week, a 30-minute session to run through technical questions would be helpful.

Marissa's quick answers (vendor-facing summary):
- SOC2 coverage: the PDF is the most recent Type II covering Jan 1 2026 - Jun 30 2026. We'll confirm the auditor and control details in the package we upload to Drive.
- Customer KMS: Redwood supports KMS integration for Dedicated and Private via BYOK patterns; for Dedicated we can accept AWS KMS keys with a key policy tied to the customer's AWS account. Private (VPC/on-prem) supports more customized HSM/KMS deployments.
- Minimum Dedicated term / provisioning: minimum 3-month reserved commit for Dedicated; typical provisioning lead time 5-10 business days after contract and infra approval. Longer commitments available for discounted pricing.

Laura / Marissa — quick technical confirmation and next steps from Security: 

- SOC2: confirmed Type II period Jan 1 2026 - Jun 30 2026; auditor is ClearRisk LLC (listed in the SOC2 PDF). We will also provide a short cover letter that maps questionnaire questions to controls (SOC2_coverage_map.docx to be uploaded).
- BYOK / KMS: Dedicated supports AWS KMS with customer-managed keys (we use an IAM role and restricted key policy for the dedicated tenant). Private supports KMS + HSM integrations for customers who need on-prem key custody.
- PHI-eligible deployment modes: 
  * Hosted (multi-tenant Redwood API): not permitted for PHI workloads.
  * Redwood Dedicated (tenant-isolated, reserved GPUs): permitted with BYOK and egress controls — typical for pilot customers.
  * Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem): permitted, recommended when Carex requires strict network boundary controls or air-gapped evidence.
- Evidence for questionnaire: we'll prepare the following artifacts for the Drive link: SOC2_Report_2026.pdf, SOC2_coverage_map.docx, network_diagram_dedicated.png, encryption_in_transit_at_rest.pdf, retention_policy_excerpt.txt, and a configuration checklist for Dedicated provisioning.

Action items: 
1) Laura: send DocuSign link for BAA (I'll review once signed).
2) Marissa: upload the evidence bundle to the shared Drive folder and flag any open questionnaire items that require legal/infra input.
3) Carex: confirm Dedicated vs Private preference and provide procurement contact for initial SOW/commit discussion.

I'll be available for the 30-min call next week.
